service.description: Text a number: the room of the current user's number fromNumber (one they are granted that has messaging; their only one when empty) and toNumber, found or made, with the user in it; several numbers in toNumber (comma-separated, at most the number's provider's group maximum: Telnyx 8) are a group text, one room for that set of numbers (plans/Comms-Messaging.md §9, group texts). Refusals carry reasonCode: notSignedIn, badNumber, emergency, numberNotGranted, noMessaging, internationalNotEnabled, premiumNotEnabled, tooManyNumbers, groupTextsNotSupported (the provider carries no group texts).

The current user's names of outside numbers (numbers comma-separated, or numberList; at most 50), from the call-context providers of the apps they may open (the first contact's name each gives): nameMap, number to name, a number no app knows left out. Only the numbers of phone rooms the user is in are asked, and at most 600 numbers an hour a user (past that none: reasonCode rateLimited). The phone rooms' names on the server's side (plans/Comms-Messaging.md §9, Phone book); the app puts the phone's own contacts first.
The numbers the current user may text from: their caller-ID grants, and their ring groups' numbers, that have a messaging bridge (numberList: phoneNumber, description).

Internal: the external room (CrtExternal) of our number and theirs, with its ChatRoomBridge on our number's messaging bridge (externalRoomId ours/theirs), found or made under the number's row lock, and the users our number reaches (its user or ring group, and its caller-ID grants) members of it; one who left stays out. reasonCode noMessaging when our number has no messaging bridge. Called in a transaction of its own before a text is taken in and before a call links to it. With theirNumberList of two or more outside numbers, the group text's room of that set (externalRoomId ours/a,b,c, the numbers in E.164 and sorted; at most the bridge's group maximum, its adapter's get#BridgeCapabilities groupMax, else tooManyNumbers; groupTextsNotSupported on a bridge whose provider carries none).

Internal (the adapter before each send, and send#SmsMessage): whether a text from fromNumber to toNumber may go now, from userId (empty: the system). allowed, else reasonCode and message: noMessaging, badNumber, emergency, numberNotGranted, internationalNotEnabled, premiumNotEnabled, optedOut, consentRequired (isPromotional with no sms-consent provider saying yes: an app's, or one a component's conf registers, asked for the system too), dailyLimit (the user's and all users' texts, or the system's own; a promotional text also its number's smsMaxPromotionalPerNumber, and one with no user that alone, not the system's). Out also the numbers in E.164 and the bridge.

parameter.name: reserve
parameter.description: Count the text for the day's limits when it is allowed, in the same step as the check under the lock of the day's deployment count (sends at once cannot pass a limit together); release#SmsSend takes it back when the text does not reach the provider

parameter.name: counterDay
parameter.description: With reserve, the day it was counted on (for release#SmsSend)

service.description: Internal: a text went to the provider (taken, or not known): it counts for the day of userId (empty: the system's) and of the deployment (SmsSendCount).

parameter.name: fromNumber
parameter.description: With isPromotional, the number whose promotional count it is

service.description: Internal: a text check#SmsSend reserved on counterDay (today when empty) for userId (empty: the system) did not reach the provider (refused, or to be tried again): it no longer counts.

parameter.name: fromNumber
parameter.description: With isPromotional, the number whose promotional count it was

service.description: Internal: a person sent keyword STOP (opted out of our number), START (back in) or HELP (kept).

Internal (an SMS adapter's webhook, after it checked the provider's signature): the provider tells that theirNumber opted out of ourNumber (keyword STOP) or back in (START), as its event eventId on bridge chatBridgeId. Applied once: the event is kept as a done ChatBridgeInbound (transactionId signal:eventId), so a copy of it (a provider with no timestamp in its signature, Twilio, can be replayed after the replay cache let it go) is outcome duplicate and changes nothing. ourNumber must have messaging through chatBridgeId (else outcome ignored, reasonCode unknownNumber). Out: outcome noted, duplicate or ignored.

Internal (an SMS adapter's webhook, after it checked the provider's signature): a text from theirNumber to ourNumber on bridge chatBridgeId, the provider's webhook eventId (the ingest transaction: a repeated webhook does nothing again) and messageId, text and mediaList [{url, contentType, fileName, maxBytes}]. A STOP, START or HELP keeps the pair's opt-out; the pair room is found or made; the text goes through ChatBridgeServices.ingest#Event. outcome (accepted, duplicate, rejected, waiting, ignored for a number without messaging on this bridge, failed), reasonCode, chatRoomId, eventSeq. recipientList, every number a group text went to (our number among them): its room is the group's, of the sender and the others. externalThreadId, the provider's conversation the text came in (a Twilio Conversation): the room of the bridge's mapping that keeps it (store#MappingThread), whoever writes. metadata, an RCS message's place (location: latitude, longitude, label, address) and tapped suggestion (postback), kept on the message; a place with no words is said as its text with a map link (an RCS bridge's: plans/Comms-Messaging.md §16).
